review_notes: I read all 83 lines of the target and inspected the main dependencies: TauCeti/Algebra/Category/GradedModuleCat/CartanMap/SimpleBasis.lean, TauCeti/Algebra/Category/GradedModuleCat/Idempotent/Head.lean, TauCeti/Algebra/Category/GradedModuleCat/CartanMap/Idempotent/Coordinate.lean, and Mathlib's definitions of Basis and CompleteOrthogonalIdempotents. The target is a thin assembly file: gradedIdempotentHeadBasis is built directly from gradedSimpleClassBasis, and the two simp lemmas are immediate specialisations of gradedSimpleClassBasis_apply and gradedSimpleClassBasis_repr_apply. I found no declaration whose hypotheses can be usefully weakened without changing the surrounding API. Replacing Field k by a weaker scalar structure is blocked because finrank-based graded dimensions and gradedIdempotentCoordinate require a field/division-ring style setting, while the Laurent coefficient ring ℤ[q,q⁻¹] is intrinsic to LaurentK0. Dropping Module.Finite k A is not sound: even with A₀ spanned by a single idempotent, an infinite-dimensional nonnegatively graded algebra such as k[x] in degree grading has a finite module A whose class is not in the ℤ[q,q⁻¹]-span of the head class. Dropping Fintype I is blocked by CompleteOrthogonalIdempotents and by the finite-sum argument in the exhaustiveness theorem. One could replace CompleteOrthogonalIdempotents by OrthogonalIdempotents together with a derived completeness proof using hspan and 1 ∈ 𝒜 0, but because hspan is still required this does not enlarge the class of applicable instances; it is merely an unpacking of the same hypotheses, so I do not count it as a useful generalisation under the rubric. The apply and repr lemmas inherit every hypothesis from the definition whose value they describe, so no separate weakening is available.
